raw_response:
I am 65 this year, and I have been farming these fields in Quzhou for 45 years. I finished primary school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and do my accounts, but I learned how to farm by doing it and watching my father and neighbors. My farm is 18.8 mu, and I work it alone — my household is just me now. I plant wheat and maize on 14 mu in rotation, and I keep 4.8 mu for cotton. Cotton can pay better, but at my age I cannot handle too much of it — the picking and spraying takes too much labor, and I have to hire help for the busy times.

For the wheat: I sow in October. I rotary till the land first. I use improved seed, the kind from the county supply store — varieties like Lumai that I have used for years. For fertilizer, I put down one bag of 18-22-5 compound fertilizer per mu as base, that is 50 kg. At green-up in March, I topdress with another half bag plus some urea. All together that works out to about 21 kg of nitrogen, 11 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate four times from my well: winter water, jointing, heading, and one more in late May if the sky stays dry. I spray pesticide three times — herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice in spring. Last year I got about 1000 jin per mu; this year I expect around 1050 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For the maize: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed, Denghai or Nongda, one package per mu. There is no time to plough, so I use no-tillage and broadcast the seed. I put one bag of 28-6-6 compound per mu as base, about 50 kg. That is about 14 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium. I do not topdress much because summer rain usually helps. I irrigate twice — at tasseling and grain filling. I spray three times: herbicide once, insecticide twice for armyworm. Yield should be about 1150 kg per mu.

For the cotton: I plant 4.8 mu in late April. I use improved seed, about 2 to 3 jin per mu. I rotary till first. Cotton needs more fertilizer than grain. I put about 100 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, split between base and when it flowers. That is about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times. But cotton has bugs all summer — bollworm, aphids, red spiders. I spray every 10 to 15 days, so about 12 times total. That costs money, but if I do not spray, I lose the whole crop. I hope for 550 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I watch what my neighbors do. The ones who got good yields last year used similar amounts. Fertilizer is expensive now, but I would rather put a bit too much than risk a bad harvest — a bad year means disaster, wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I am old and alone, so I hire young workers for cotton picking and some spraying, but I make all the decisions myself. I do not try new methods unless I saw them work on someone else's field first.
